newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to name expert to examine Belgian closure.
newsitem.headline: Renault to name expert to examine Belgian closure.

text.p: French carmaker Renault will name an independent expert to examine alternatives to the planned closure of its Vilvoorde plant who will have to report back within a month, French afternoon daily Le Monde said on Tuesday.

The expert will look at such options as cutting working hours and reducing costs to save the plant, the newspaper said. The Renault board would meet to decide whether to go ahead with the closure after the expert made his recommendations.
The newspaper said Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer would announce what it described as the "face-saving" decision to the company's board of directors and shareholders' at meetings later on Tuesday.

It said that two experts who had been approached had already refused the task because they knew that they would reach the same conclusion as Renault -- that the Renault plant closure, set for July 31, was inevitable.

Facing fierce European competition, Renault, which lost 5.25 billion francs last year, has insisted the plant must close to streamline its money-losing car assembly operations and cut costs. Otherwise "the company will die", Schweitzer has said.
Renault has already said shorter work weeks are not a solution to Renault's need to bring its scattered production operations in line with those of its competitors in Europe.
